description: Every traveller goes through primary inspection. Some are sent to secondary. One legal account puts roughly 5% of arrivals as referred at random, with many more referred for cause - a database hit, a watchlist match, a travel-pattern anomaly, a social media flag, a tip from another agency, or an unresolved prior immigration record.
energy_note: Five per cent at random, and then the rest for reasons.

aspect: What the visa actually entitles you to
description: A visa permits travel to a port of entry and a request for admission. It does not guarantee entry; an officer at the port decides admissibility after arrival, regardless of the years spent obtaining the visa.
energy_note: Every approval you obtained, overridable at the desk.

description: Waiting hours, missing connections, being asked the same question repeatedly while officers review prior entries, visa applications, arrests and petitions. Inspections run from 30 minutes to many hours.
money_note: Missed connections and rebooked flights, per occurrence.
energy_note: Four hours, and the connecting flight is gone.

aspect: Your phone is searchable without a warrant
description: At a port of entry, Fourth and Fifth Amendment protections are sharply reduced. CBP can search phones without a warrant under the border search exception, and can send visa holders home on the next flight.
energy_note: Your messages, read, lawfully, while you wait.

aspect: HONEST GAP - there is no published per-nationality rate
description: No systematic data or civil-rights finding was located showing Nigerian travellers are disproportionately referred to secondary. The publicly available CBP material on Nigerians is agency-published enforcement cases, which is not evidence of a pattern. The disparity is widely reported by travellers and is not, at present, a published statistic.
energy_note: Everybody experiences the rate. Nobody publishes it.
notes: Handled the same way as AIR-001 in assets/text/palestine. Stating the gap is more useful than inventing a number.

aspect: So the adaptation is defensive and permanent
description: Arrive four hours early. Never book a tight connection. Carry the invitation letter, the bank statements, the return ticket and the hotel booking in print. Assume the phone will be read. This is unpaid preparation performed before every single journey.
money_note: Annual cost of defensive travel planning.
energy_note: Packing for an interrogation, every time.

aspect: SCENARIO - the four hours at Atlanta
description: She is referred at 06:40. Her connection to Raleigh is at 09:15. At 09:50 an officer returns her passport, says nothing further, and points at the exit. The airline rebooks her for 18:20 and charges the change fee, because the delay was not the airline's.
energy_note: Cleared, with no explanation, and billed for the delay.

description: Print everything. Arrive absurdly early. Never book a connection under three hours. Assume the phone will be read, so curate it beforehand. After a decade this is no longer a set of precautions; it is simply how the person travels, and they no longer notice they are doing it.
energy_note: Defensive travel, absorbed into the character.
